s.t:
Seven Education entwickelt eine intelligente, KI‑gestützte Plattform, die Schulen und Bildungseinrichtungen hilft, effizienter zu arbeiten. Unsere Produkte reduzieren administrative Aufgaben, verbessern die Kommunikation und ermöglichen es Lehrkräften, Institutionen und Bildungsverantwortlichen, sich auf das zu konzentrieren, was wirklich zählt: Lernen, Wachstum und Menschen.
Als europäische EdTech‑Gruppe mit über 350 Mitarbeitenden bauen wir intuitive, skalierbare Lösungen, die den Alltag von Schulen und Bildungseinrichtungen erleichtern. Unsere Software schafft jeden Tag Klarheit, vereinfacht Abläufe und stärkt die Zusammenarbeit.

Wir handeln mit Mut, Ownership und echter Zusammenarbeit – und lassen uns von dem Impact inspirieren, den unsere Produkte für die Menschen schaffen, die das Herzstück der Bildung sind. Unser Ziel ist klar: die führende EdTech‑Marke Europas zu werden.
Wenn du Teil dieser Reise werden und mit uns wachsen möchtest, freuen wir uns sehr, von dir zu hören.
Aufgaben

Als Working Student People Operations bei Seven Education gestaltest du unseren HR-Alltag im DACH-Raum aktiv mit, von der sorgfältigen Datenpflege bis zur Begleitung einzelner Schritte im Employee Lifecycle. Du übernimmst früh eigene Aufgaben und bekommst einen realistischen Einblick, wie operatives HR-Management in einem wachsenden, internationalen EdTech-Unternehmen funktioniert. Dabei hilfst du mit, unsere HR-Prozesse zu digitalisieren und weiterzuentwickeln.

HR-Alltag mit echtem Einfluss: Du pflegst Personaldaten in Personio, bearbeitest Anfragen von Mitarbeitenden und kümmerst dich um wiederkehrende Vorgänge wie Vertragsanpassungen oder Elternzeitanträge. Du unterstützt dabei, dass die operativen Abläufe im Hintergrund zuverlässig laufen.
Employee Lifecycle von Anfang bis Ende: Du begleitest Mitarbeitende durch alle Stationen, vom Onboarding neuer Kolleg:innen bis zum Offboarding, und unterstützt unsere People Operations Manager:innen bei allem, was dazwischen liegt. Dazu gehört auch die eigenständige Erstellung von Arbeitszeugnissen und HR-Dokumenten.
Daten, auf die man sich verlassen kann: Du erstellst Reports und Auswertungen in unserem HRIS Personio und übernimmst die Verantwortung für die Datenqualität. Zahlen sind für dich kein notwendiges Übel, sondern ein echtes Werkzeug.
Prozesse denken, Strukturen bauen: Du bringst dich aktiv in die Digitalisierung und Weiterentwicklung unserer HR-Prozesse ein, etwa durch den Aufbau und die Pflege von Confluence-Seiten oder die Optimierung der Personio-Struktur. Ein fester Teil deiner Zeit gehört solchen Projekten.
Qualifikation

Studium mit Bezug zur Rolle: Du studierst HR, BWL, Psychologie oder ein verwandtes Fach und bist noch mindestens ein Jahr eingeschrieben.
People Ops Erfahrung: Du hast bereits erste Einblicke in HR-Operations gesammelt, durch Praktika, Werkstudierendenjobs oder vergleichbare Tätigkeiten. Auch Erfahrungen aus Sachbearbeitung oder Executive Assistenz sind willkommen.
Umgang mit sensiblen Daten: Mit vertraulichen Personaldaten gehst du selbstverständlich sorgfältig und diskret um.
Datenaffinität: Du arbeitest gern mit Zahlen und Stammdaten, präzise und detailorientiert, und behältst auch bei vielen parallelen Aufgaben den Überblick.
Eigenständige Arbeitsweise: Du setzt Aufgaben zuverlässig um, denkst dabei mit und bringst eigene Vorschläge ein. Mit unklaren oder wechselnden Situationen kommst du gut zurecht.
Sprachlich sicher: Dein Deutsch ist fließend, schriftlich wie mündlich. Auf Englisch kommunizierst du sicher genug für die Zusammenarbeit in einem internationalen Team.
Von Vorteil: Erfahrung mit HRIS-Systemen (z. B. Personio), Kenntnisse im DACH-Kontext (AT/CH) oder Erfahrung in Datenanalyse und Reporting.

Work-Life-Balance: Volle 30 Tage Urlaub (bei einer 5-Tage-Woche) plus zusätzlich jeweils einen halben freien Tag an Heiligabend und Silvester.
Flexibilität: Wir bieten dir die Möglichkeit entweder 16 oder 20 Wochenstunden zu arbeiten. Du arbeitest hybrid: das heißt, du kombinierst Arbeit im Home Office mit regelmäßigen Tagen im Büro.
Sinnhaftigkeit: Wir digitalisieren Bildung – deine Arbeit leistet einen echten gesellschaftlichen Beitrag.
Team & Culture: Wir leben eine Kultur auf Augenhöhe. Dich erwarten ein Teambuilding-Budget für Events, Workation-Möglichkeiten im EU-Ausland und eine herzliche Atmosphäre.
Dog Friendly: Dein Vierbeiner ist im Büro herzlich willkommen!

Deine Aufgaben
Standort: München, hybrid (2 Tage/Woche im Office, Rest remote) · Befristet bis Ende Februar 2028 · 30–40 Stunden/Woche
Für unser People & Organization Team in München suchen wir einen Senior People Operations Specialist (m/w/d) zur Vertretung während einer Elternzeit, befristet bis Ende Februar 2028. Diese individual Contributor (IC) Rolle berichtet direkt an den VP People & Organization und hat ihren Schwerpunkt auf Deutschland.
Du übernimmst gemeinsam mit unserer bestehenden People Operations Managerin die operative Verantwortung für People Operations und stellst operative Exzellenz im Employee Lifecycle sicher. Du agierst eigenständig auf Senior-Niveau, bringst tiefe fachliche Expertise mit und übernimmst Verantwortung für komplexe Workstreams unserer P&O-Agenda.
Du fungierst als erfahrene Stimme im Team und bringst eigene Standards für Qualität, Compliance und Employee Experience ein.
Du verantwortest komplexe und sensible Themen im Employee Lifecycle eigenständig, von schwierigen Vertragssituationen über Sonderkonstellationen bis zu mehrdeutigen Befristungs-, Teilzeit- oder Elternzeitfällen.
Du bist fachlicher Ansprechpartner für vertragliche und sozialversicherungsrechtliche Fragestellungen und arbeitest souverän mit externen Beratern (z.B. Steuerberater, Anwaltskanzlei).
Du treibst den Aufbau unserer Compliance-Themen (Datenschutz, Mutterschutz, etc.) eigenverantwortlich voran und steuerst die Umsetzung mit hoher Eigenständigkeit.
Du leitest komplexe P&O-OKR-Workstreams und Projekte mit Gestaltungsspielraum von Konzeption bis Rollout und gestaltest die Weiterentwicklung unserer Prozesse durch Technologie und KI aktiv mit.
Du übernimmst Sparring und Mentoring für weniger erfahrene Kollegen im Team.
Was Du mitbringst
Abgeschlossenes Studium im Bereich BWL, Psychologie, Personalmanagement, Arbeitsrecht oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung.
Mindestens 6 Jahre Berufserfahrung in der operativen Personalarbeit, idealerweise in einem dynamischen, internationalen Umfeld mit hybrider oder remote Arbeitsweise, inkl. eigenverantwortlicher Steuerung von HR-Projekten (z.B. Compliance-Aufbau, Systemmigration oder Prozessoptimierung).
Fundierte Kenntnisse im deutschen Arbeits- und Sozialversicherungsrecht. Du kannst komplexe Fälle eigenständig einschätzen, inkl. Kündigungsschutz, AGG-Vorgängen und sozialversicherungsrechtlichen Fragen.
Erweiterte Kenntnisse im Umgang mit KI-Tools im HR-Kontext.
Hohe inhaltliche Eigenständigkeit, ausgeprägtes Urteilsvermögen und Sicherheit im Umgang mit sensiblen Themen und Stakeholdern auf Leitungsebene. Diskretion, professionelle Distanz, klare Kommunikation und Freude an Aufbauarbeit.
Verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse und gute bis sehr gute Englischkenntnisse.
Was wir Dir bieten
Verantwortungsvolle, spannende und abwechslungsreiche Aufgaben mit viel Gestaltungsspielraum in einem dynamischen Unternehmen , das flache Hierarchien und eine offene, lockere Arbeitsatmosphäre lebt, in der alle per "Du" sind
Ein freundliches, offenes Team bestehend aus ca. 450 Mitarbeitenden in Deutschland, UK und Belgien mit mehreren lieben Bürohunden an unseren Standorten
Flexible Arbeitszeiten (die auf Vertrauensarbeitszeit basieren), Home-Office Optionen inkl. Kostenbeteiligung an Deiner Home-Office Ausstattung und die Möglichkeit, für mehrere Monate aus dem Ausland zu arbeiten
28 Tage Urlaubsanspruch sowie die Möglichkeit, bis zu 20 Tage unbezahlten Urlaub sowie Sonderurlaub zu nehmen!
Zugang zu modernen KI-Tools: Wir stellen Dir moderne KI-Tools zur Verfügung, die Dich dabei unterstützen, effizienter zu arbeiten, neue Ideen zu entwickeln und Deine Fähigkeiten in einer sich stetig wandelnden digitalen Welt weiter auszubauen.
Verschiedene interne & externe Weiterentwicklungsmöglichkeiten , die Du eigenständig nach Deinen Interessen auswählen kannst
Deine mentale Gesundheit ist uns wichtig! Deshalb kannst Du im Rahmen der Plattform " OpenUp " anonym an Einzel- oder Gruppentherapie-Sitzungen teilnehmen oder in 1:1 Meetings mit echten Therapeuten sprechen
EGYM Wellpass Mitgliedschaft: Mit unserer bezuschussten Mitgliedschaft beim EGYM Wellpass erhältst Du Zugang zu tausenden Sport- und Wellnesseinrichtungen – darunter Fitnessstudios, Schwimmbäder, Kletterhallen, Yoga- und Pilatesstudios sowie viele weitere Angebote. So kannst Du flexibel und deutschlandweit etwas für Deine Fitness und Dein Wohlbefinden tun – ganz so, wie es am besten in Deinen Alltag passt!
Verschiedene Mitarbeiterrabatte - für Mensch und Tier!
Regelmäßige Team-, Company- und Family & Friends- Events
Du brauchst eine Pause? Entspanne Dich in unserer Social-Area, die mit einem Kicker ausgestattet ist oder fordere Deine Kollegen auf unserer gemütlichen Sofalandschaft zu einem Mario Kart-Battle (oder einem anderen Nintendo Switch Spiel) heraus!
Aufgewärmtes Essen magst Du nicht? Essen bestellen dauert Dir zu lange? In unserem Büro steht Dir eine hochwertige, vollausgestattete Küche zur Verfügung in der Du den Kochlöffel schwingen oder tolle Kuchen zaubern kannst!
Kaffee, Kakao, Tee und weitere kühle Softdrinks wie Wasser und Säfte sowie frisches Obst, kleinere Snacks und eine prall gefüllte Süßigkeiten-Schublade stehen Dir kostenlos zur Verfügung
Viele weitere, großartige Benefits die wir Dir gerne im Rahmen des Recruitingprozesses näher vorstellen!

Human Resources Generalist (Remote)

Provide HR services to support candidates, employees, and managers across multiple locations. Manage key HR processes such as employment offers, onboarding, employee relations, policies, leaves of absence, and terminations, utilizing HRIS systems.

Collaborate with recruitment on hiring and updates, coordinate meetings with managers, conduct exit interviews, and assist with benefits and employee issues. Support and potentially back-up HR management functions related to HRIS, benefits, and performance management.

Foster strong relationships across the organization, ensuring efficient HR operations in a virtual environment.

Bachelor’s degree in HR, Business, or related field with 3-5 years of relevant experience, especially in hiring, onboarding, and HRIS.
Strong HRIS proficiency (preferably UKG).
Experience with investigations, corrective actions, and terminations preferred.
Excellent communication and customer service skills.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, virtual setting.
Knowledge of employment laws and compliance.
Self-motivated, detail-oriented, and adaptable to organizational needs.

You will interpret current and proposed military personnel action regulations to determine the impact on an organization.
You will evaluate human resource workforce performance to identify training and development needs for employees.
You will analyze qualitative and quantitative data to report human capital management statistical information to managers.
You will consult with customers on human resources issues (e.g., strategic workforce development, sustainment, compensation management, organizational design).
You will develop a strategic staffing plan to meet future workforce needs.
Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-07 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1) Review pay and personnel allowances & entitlements in accordance with laws and regulations; 2) Ensure records maintenance is performed in automated personnel systems for quality assurance and/or Monitor personnel actions (e.g. separations, transfers, and retirements) for inclusion in the Official Military Personnel File (OMPF); 3) Utilize various automated systems to verify pay and personnel actions; 4) Identify gaps in workflow processes and Establish workload to achieve efficiency of operations; 5) Advise customers on policy concerning pay and personnel accounts and resolve complex pay and personnel questions and issues; and 6) Reviews transactions submitted to update service member's pay and personnel records.

NOTE: This information must be fully supported in your resume to be considered for the position.

Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management web site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/#url=List-by-Occupational-Series https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/0200/human-resources-management-series-0201/ Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

As a GS- 0201-15, your typical work assignments may include the following: Supervises HR Specialists and support staff. Assigns and reviews work, sets priorities, evaluates performance, and addresses staffing, conduct, and training needs. Provides coaching and development to build staff capability and ensure high-quality service delivery.

Leads HR accountability and quality assurance activities across the Division. Develops standardized HR processes, procedures, and internal controls to ensure consistency, efficiency, and compliance.

Conducts internal audits and reviews of HR programs and personnel actions, identifies risks and improvement opportunities, and recommends corrective actions. Develops performance measures to evaluate HR service quality and effectiveness. Directs HR staff development programs, including training, mentoring, and career development initiatives.

Designs competency models and training programs across HR functional areas. Identifies skill gaps and develops strategies to strengthen long-term HR workforce capability, including succession planning. Leads Division-wide employee and leadership development programs for attorneys, paralegals, supervisors, and managers.

Develops and delivers training programs, onboarding, and leadership development initiatives. Coordinates blended learning approaches and evaluates program effectiveness to improve workforce capability. Supports HR strategic planning and organizational improvement initiatives.

Conducts workforce analyses, identifies capability gaps, and develops recommendations to improve effectiveness and efficiency. Leads or supports special projects and provides analytical reports and dashboards to senior leadership.
To qualify for the GS-15 level, applicants must have one year of specialized experience in the Federal service. Specialized experience is experience that has equipped the applicant with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position.

Specialized experience for this position includes: Leading or managing human resources programs such as workforce planning, employee development, leadership development, or HR operations; Developing or improving HR policies, procedures, or processes to improve efficiency, consistency, or compliance with applicable laws and agency requirements; Advising senior leaders on human resources issues involving workforce needs, program performance, or organizational effectiveness; and Leading or supervising HR staff, contractors, or teams performing HR-related work.

Examples of qualifying experience may include: leading HR improvement efforts across an organization, developing training or development programs for employees or supervisors, or managing HR initiatives that improve how a large organization operates.

You MUST meet all qualification requirements, including Time-in-Grade, by the closing date of this announcement, Your resume must support your responses to the online questionnaire and the qualification requirements. Failure to do so may result in an ineligible rating.

See the Required Documents section for important notes about what must be included in your resume.

This Human Resources Specialist (Operations) position is located Human Capital/Operations, Transportation Security Administration, Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

Duties include but are not limited to: Provides advice and guidance to management, employees, and stakeholders on human capital operational programs, including personnel action processing, payroll administration, time and attendance, personnel records management, onboarding, offboarding, and complex personnel matters.

Processes, reviews, and resolves a wide range of human resources actions and operational issues, including personnel actions, pay and compensation matters, benefits-related transactions, leave programs, employment records, debt bills, retroactive corrections, and other actions affecting an employee's federal service history.

Conducts analysis of reports, system data, records, metrics, and case information to identify processing errors, operational problems, trends, or programmatic weaknesses; documents findings, performs root cause analysis, and recommends corrective actions.

Maintains, reviews, and safeguards personnel-related records and documentation in accordance with federal records management, privacy, and security requirements; ensures records are complete, accurate, retrievable, and properly handled.

Researches and resolves complex, sensitive, retroactive, or high-profile human capital operational issues involving areas such as pay, benefits, personnel processing, incentives, severance, workers' compensation, unemployment compensation, leave transfer, and other specialized employee matters.

Serves as a liaison with internal program offices, servicing providers, and external partners; develops and updates standard operating procedures, job aids, guidance, briefings, presentations, and training materials to support consistent and compliant HC Operations processes.

Please note: The major duties are at the full performance level, SV-I band.

Program Section Summaries: Document Management: The Document Management team is responsible for organizing, storing, and safeguarding all personnel-related documents in accordance with federal records management requirements, managing HR document systems by setting government-wide rules for personnel records and using the electronic Official Personnel Folder (eOPF).

They maintain legal and financial employment histories for civil service workers, standardize document workflows, and facilitate efficient retrieval and secure handling of sensitive information to support operational needs Payroll: The Payroll team provides payroll administration and compensation activities, interpreting and applying rules, laws, and policies to ensure accurate pay for federal employees, including pay-impacting programs such as unemployment, workers' compensation, and Voluntary Leave Transfer.

They deliver authoritative guidance to managers and employees on complex compensation issues - including basic pay, overtime, leave entitlements, and debt bills - while monitoring payroll reports and completing payment processing to ensure timely notification and resolution for the agency and affected individuals.

Personnel Processing: The Personnel Processing team manages all aspects of onboarding, offboarding, and personnel actions for federal employees, ensuring compliance with applicable policies and regulations.

They manage the formal system for documenting, approving, and tracking changes in a federal employee's career using standardized forms such as the SF-52 and SF-50, and ensure all personnel actions are accurately recorded and maintained throughout federal service.

Special Handling: The Special Handling team addresses unique, retroactive, or complex personnel cases that fall outside standard processing procedures, handling specialized cases across all areas of human capital, including benefits, severance, pay, processing, and incentives.

They also provide expert support for other agency needs on sensitive and high-profile actions, applying specialized expertise to resolve non-routine issues and ensure compliance with federal guidelines for exceptional cases.
In addition to the minimum qualifications described above, you must meet the following specialized experience and/or education requirement to be considered qualified for the position: To qualify for the SV-G Pay Band (equivalent to GS-11), you must have one year of specialized experience at the SV-F or GS-09 in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private sector.

Specialized experience is defined as experience that has equipped you with the knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position.

Specialized experience is defined as: Experience assisting with human resources operational functions such as personnel action processing, payroll support, time and attendance administration, benefits-related processing, employee records management, onboarding, or offboarding activities.

Experience communicating with internal (i.e. employees, managers) and external stakeholders regarding human resources processes, procedures, forms, records, or transaction status.

Experience utilizing an automated human resource, payroll, timekeeping, or records systems to enter, retrieve, update, track, or validate employee information (i.e GovTA, WebTA).

OR In lieu of experience, you must possess the education requirement for this band level: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or LL.M., if related. OR A combination of education and experience.

To qualify for the SV-H Pay Band (equivalent to GS-12), you must have one year of specialized experience at the SV-G or GS-11 in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private sector.

Specialized experience is defined as experience that has equipped you with the knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position.

Specialized experience is defined as: Experience interpreting and applying human resources laws, regulations, policies, and procedures to support personnel action processing, payroll administration, time and attendance, benefits-related transactions, records management, or other human capital operational functions.

Experience reviewing, processing, or resolving human resources actions, such as personnel actions, pay-related transactions, onboarding or offboarding actions, leave-related matters, employment records updates, or benefits-related documentation.

Experience researching and responding to inquiries from internal (i.e. employees, managers) and external stakeholders regarding human resources operational issues, policies, procedures, records, or system-related actions.

To qualify for the SV-I Pay Band (equivalent to GS-13), you must have one year of specialized experience at the SV-H or GS-12 in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private sector.

Specialized experience is defined as experience that has equipped you with the knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position.

Specialized experience is defined as: Experience processing, reviewing, or resolving unprecedented human resources actions involving pay, leave, benefits-related transactions, personnel records, retroactive corrections, onboarding, offboarding, or other employee lifecycle actions.

Experience analyzing reports, system data, metrics, case files, or personnel records to identify processing errors, trends, operational problems, compliance issues, or programmatic weaknesses and recommending corrective actions.

Experience providing technical guidance to employees, supervisors, managers, HR staff, timekeepers, financial specialists, or other stakeholders on human resources operational requirements, procedures, and case resolution.

Experience developing or updating standard operating procedures, job aids, guidance, briefings, or training materials related to human capital operational processes. Credit for experience is given based on a 40-hour workweek.

Part-time experience is credited on a part-time ratio, i.e., working 20 hours per week for two months equals one month of experience. No additional credit is given for overtime.

National Service Experience (i.e., volunteer experience): Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees.

If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office.

You must meet the qualification requirements for this position no later than the closing date of the vacancy announcement.

Leads team members by distributing work, tracking progress, communicating priorities, and supporting training, problem solving, and work planning. Provides technical support for processing personnel actions, including appointments, promotions, adjustments, realignments, and reorganizations.

Reviews personnel action documentation, resolves incomplete or incorrect data, and identifies corrective actions for non-routine processing issues. Reconstructs employment history and reviews records to verify service computation dates, career tenure, pay-setting, and record accuracy.

Supports personnel recordkeeping by tracking documents, resolving pending cases, and recommending improvements to records processes. Coordinates with payroll, benefits, staffing, and customer agencies to support onboarding, personnel processing, and employee records services.

Provides project support by sharing service data, production statistics, process input, and technical guidance for reimbursable HR services.
For the GS 12: You must have at least one year (52 weeks, full-time) of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 level in the Federal service (or comparable level of experience from outside the Federal service) performing ALL the following duties: Leading or coordinating the work of human resources staff responsible for processing federal personnel actions utilizing federal HRIT systems and/or maintaining official personnel records; Processing or reviewing personnel actions using human resources systems and formalized guidance such as the Guide to Processing Personnel Actions (GPPA); Reviewing official personnel folders or electronic personnel records to verify required documentation, identify missing or inaccurate federal employment data, and determine corrective action; and Advising managers, human resources staff, employees, payroll, benefits, or other functional areas on personnel processing, recruitment and placement, pay administration, benefits impacts, or records management requirements.

Merit promotion applicants must meet the time-in-grade requirement as defined in 5 CFR 300, Subpart F. One year at the GS-11 level is required to meet the time-in-grade requirements for the GS12 level. You must meet all qualification and eligibility requirements within 30 days of the closing date of this announcement.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

As a Human Resources Specialist in the Executive Resources Division, you will: Support and administer human capital programs for Senior Executive Service (SES) members, Senior Level (SL) employees, Administrative Law Judges (ALJs), Intergovernmental Personnel Act (IPA) Mobility Program detailees, and political appointees, including Presidential appointees, non-career SES, and Schedule C positions.

Provide expert guidance on recruitment, staffing, hiring, onboarding, position management, classification, and pay administration for career and non-career executive positions.

Prepare tentatively selected executive candidates for OPM Qualifications Review Board (QRB) Structured Interviews, including coordinating with OPM, reviewing materials, and advising candidates on expectations and interview readiness. Assist selectees in assembling qualification materials and transitioning effectively into the agency.

Coordinate and prepare documentation, analysis, recommendations, and decision-ready materials for the Executive Resources Board (ERB), Performance Review Board (PRB), and senior leadership.

Support executive compensation activities, including salary-setting packages, pay adjustments, incentives, compensation modeling, and coordination with legal, budget, or OPM partners as required.

Maintain and update Executive Resources information systems, including the Executive and Schedule C System (ESCS), ensuring accurate tracking of executive hiring actions, personnel movements, and government-wide compliance.

Manage or support executive performance management processes using USA Performance, including plan initiation, mid-year reviews, close-out activities, awards submissions, data calls, and compliance with OPM and OMB requirements.

Conduct studies, evaluations, and special projects related to executive personnel programs; develop or revise internal guidance, policies, procedures, and operational processes.

Collaborate across FTC bureaus and offices; coordinate intergovernmental assignments, executive details, and executive onboarding activities; and support agency-wide initiatives impacting senior leadership.

Represent the Executive Resources Division in meetings, working groups, and negotiations; present recommendations; resolve issues; and provide advisory services on complex, sensitive, or precedent-setting executive human capital matters.

Contribute to the improvement of executive resources policies, systems, and operations to ensure effective, compliant, and strategic management of the agency's senior workforce.
To qualify for the Human Resources Specialist (Executive Resources) position at the GS-13 level, you must meet the following requirements: You must demonstrate in your resume at least one (1) year of qualifying experience equivalent to at least the GS-12 level in the Federal service obtained in either the private or public sector, performing the following types of tasks: applying Office of Personnel Management (OPM) policies and principles for SES, SL, ALJ, political appointee, and Intergovernmental Personnel Act (IPA) Mobility Program detailee staffing; assisting in policies and operations covering executive recruitment, staffing, position management, classification, performance management, executive compensation, and executive development; providing advisory support to managers and supervisors; assisting tentatively selected candidates preparing for OPM Qualifications Review Board (QRB) Structured Interviews; maintaining executive resource systems such as the Executive Schedule C System (ESCS) and USA Performance; and researching and applying laws, regulations, and policies governing executive personnel programs.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

This position is located in the Military Personnel Office (MILPO) of the Army National Guard (ARNG). The purpose of the position is to provide oversight, planning, interpretation, and application of policy.

Provide final review and validation of subordinate products for presentation to senior leadership, and produce and issue guidance to lower echelon units and commands.

Work is to be performed in one or more of the following Health Systems work areas: Tricare, Military Medical Support Office (MMSO), Line of Duty/Incapacitation (LOD/INCAP), Medical Operational Data System (MODS), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) Certification, Warrior Transition Unit/Active Duty Medical Extension/Medical Retention Processing (WTU/ADME/MRP2), and Medical boards.

At Omegga, we're on a mission to reinvent how AI and spectroscopy can drive positive change for animals, people and the planet. We started with a clear objective: eliminate chick culling on a global scale through early, non-invasive in-ovo sex detection. This outdated practice still impacts billions of lives, and we're here to change that. We're not building for the niche, we're building for the global standard.
Today, our systems are already in use, and the focus is on scaling performance, robustness, and deployment across an international customer base. For us, scaling means more than growth. It means changing an industry for the better.
We are looking for people who take ownership, think in systems, and want to help turn a working product into the industry benchmark. If that sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

You'll work directly with our Head of Finance&HRand keep the people side of Omegga running while we scale. This is not a "help out where needed" working student role. You own recurring processes end to end, and you get real responsibility from week one.
Onboarding & Offboarding: Own the operational employee lifecycle. Prepare contracts and documents, coordinate equipment and accounts, run structured first days, and manage clean offboardings.
Personio: Keep our HR system the single source of truth. Maintain employee data, absences, digital personnel files, and documentation quality, and help us get more out of the tool than we do today.
Recruiting Support: Draft and publish job ads, keep our applicant tracking system clean, coordinate interview scheduling, and own candidate communication so no application goes unanswered.
Recruiting Day: Organize our candidate day end to end: invitations, agenda, materials, interviewer briefings, and on site coordination.
Internal Events: Plan and run internal formats, from team events to company offsite
Development Budget: Take ownership of our people development budget. Build the process and guideline from scratch with us, then run it: track requests and spend, support colleagues in finding the right trainings, and keep it transparent.
Performance & Review Process: Help us prepare the rollout of our company wide review cycle. You build templates, timelines and tooling, and drive the internal communication around it.
Your Profile
Enrolled student (Bachelor or Master), around 16 hours per week during the semester, more during breaks if you want to. We plan in weeks, not fixed days, so exams and lectures can be accommodated as long as recurring processes stay covered. Ideally for at least 12 months. Your field of study is open. Business, psychology, law or something entirely different. What matters is that you care how people work in a company, not which lecture hall you sit in.
Fluent in German and English, in writing. Contracts, Personio entries and internal comms are partly German. Typos in an employment document are not a small thing.
Some practical experience in HR, recruiting or operations, ideally somewhere that moved fast. We don't need an HR certificate. We need structure and judgment.
You catch what others miss. The missing signature, the wrong start date, the empty field in Personio. In HR, sloppy data becomes someone's problem three months later.
Discretion is second nature. You handle contract and personnel data without ever making it a topic.
You'd rather fix a process than repeat it. New tools don't scare you (Personio, Ashby, Notion, Google Workspace), and manual work twice in a row makes you build something better. You close loops without being asked. You structure your own week, decide when a decision is needed, and you push back when someone tries to bend a process.
Why Us
Mission & Technical Challenge: At Omegga, you work on problems that are both technically demanding and globally relevant. We build deep-tech solutions with real-world impact, pushing the boundaries of what's currently possible.
Real Ownership: You won't be doing research tasks on the side. You run processes that the whole company touches, and you'll see the results of your work in how the whole team experiences Omegga.

Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan (ICTAP)- The ICTAP provides eligible displaced Federal competitive service employees with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies.

If your agency has notified you in writing that you are a displaced employee eligible for ICTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your ICTAP eligibility; 2) you apply under the instructions in the announcement; and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy.

To be well-qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and receive a score of 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide proof of eligibility to receive selection priority.

Such proof may include a copy of your written notification of ICTAP eligibility or a copy of your separation personnel action form. Additional information about ICTAP eligibility is at: http://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/workforce-restructuring/employee-guide-to-career-transition/.

Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP)-The CTAP provides eligible surplus and displaced competitive service employees in the Department of Justice with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies.

If your Department of Justice component has notified you in writing that you are a surplus or displaced employee eligible for CTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your CTAP eligibility, 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement, and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy.

To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and receive a score of 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.

Additional information about CTAP eligibility is at http://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/workforce-restructuring/employee-guide-to-career-transition/.

Le/la HR Generalist assure le support opérationnel RH au quotidien pour tous les salariés du site de Montreux, sous la supervision du HR Manager.

Il/elle est le point de contact de proximité des collaborateurs pour l'ensemble du cycle RH : recrutement, onboarding/offboarding, administration du personnel, gestion de la relation employé et organisation d'événements internes.

Sa mission est de garantir la fiabilité et la fluidité des processus RH, tout en contribuant aux initiatives d'engagement, de formation et de performance définies par l’équipe RH.

Support HR \& Partenariat Accompagner le HR Manager et les équipes de direction en fournissant un support RH au quotidien, aligné sur les besoins du business.
Contribuer à l'élaboration des initiatives de recrutement, de fidélisation et d'engagement des collaborateurs.
Recrutement et Intégration Accompagner les managers dans la conduite des processus de recrutement.
Assurer les tâches courantes de recrutement : publication des offres d'emploi, présélection des candidats, coordination des entretiens et préparation des offres.
Garantir une expérience d'intégration réussie, incluant la préparation du welcome kit et des programmes d'induction.
Gérer les démarches administratives liées à l'intégration et au départ des collaborateurs, en assurant des transitions fluides.
Administration du Personnel et Conformité Tenir à jour les dossiers du personnel (contrats, avenants, données personnelles), en conformité avec le droit du travail suisse et le RGPD.
Veiller au respect des lois du travail et des politiques de l'entreprise, notamment en matière de documentation, de sécurité et d'exigences légales ; remonter les problématiques au HR Manager si nécessaire.
Soutenir le HR Manager lors des audits et suivre les évolutions réglementaires.
Contribuer à la préparation des rapports et des analyses RH afin d'appuyer la prise de décision.
Collaborer étroitement avec les Spécialistes Payroll et Gestion des Temps pour garantir un suivi précis et dans les délais de la paie et des présences.
Relations et Engagement des Collaborateurs Entretenir des relations solides avec les collaborateurs en étant leur premier point de contact pour toute question ou préoccupation du quotidien.
Promouvoir une culture d'entreprise ouverte et inclusive, alignée sur les valeurs de la société.
Participer à la mise en œuvre d'initiatives visant à renforcer l'engagement, le moral et le bien\-être des collaborateurs.
Organiser et coordonner les événements internes, incluant les activités de team\-building, journées à thème et célébrations.
Gestion de la Performance et Développement des Compétences Contribuer au suivi des plans de développement de carrière des collaborateurs à haut potentiel.
Soutenir le déploiement de programmes de formation adaptés, en coordination avec le HR Manager et la CLP Academy.
Gérer l'ensemble des aspects administratifs liés aux formations.
Excellence Opérationnelle RH Veiller à ce que les processus RH soient efficaces et conformes aux objectifs de l'organisation.
Maintenir les systèmes RH à jour, en garantissant l'exactitude des données et la confidentialité.
Compiler les indicateurs RH et fournir au HR Manager des analyses exploitables.
Alignement Culturel et Valeurs Incarner les valeurs de Clinique La Prairie en les intégrant au quotidien, en favorisant une culture d'excellence, de collaboration et de respect.
Porter des initiatives favorisant l'inclusion, la diversité et une culture d'entreprise positive.
Contribuer aux programmes renforçant la mission, la vision et les valeurs de l'entreprise.

CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 40,000 students from 1,000+ universities, and our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. We've spent nearly a decade training the next generation of technical talent, and we just launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic, building one of the most ambitious AI workforce programs in the world.
We're now expanding into new markets and scaling our team so we can move at the speed AI is transforming the workforce. People joining CodePath now will have the opportunity to help architect the next frontier of our work.
We believe technical skill is the fastest way to turn raw talent into real opportunity. We train the engineers the AI era runs on, building toward millions of learners, hundreds of millions in revenue, and billions in economic impact. If you want to own something and be part of a 0-to-1 journey at an organization moving at the speed of AI, this is the place to build it.

Location: Remote (U.S.)
Role Type: Full-Time
Reporting to: Head of People

Manages: A pod of early-talent recruiters plus fractional HR coordination support
Key Activities
Claude Corps is a fellowship that places early-career technologists inside nonprofits, government agencies, and public-interest organizations to build AI solutions that keep working after the fellow leaves. It runs as a partnership between Anthropic, CodePath, and Social Finance, backed by a $150M initiative with Anthropic. CodePath is the Employer of Record: we own the full fellow lifecycle, from recruiting and selection through employment, onboarding, benefits, and host support.
Cohort 1 places 100 fellows. The program scales toward 1,000 fellows in year one and 10,000 by year three. This role builds the pod that makes that scale real.
Why this role, now
Claude Corps needs one person accountable for how fellows get hired and how they get employed. Not a strategic HR seat at a distance from the work, and not a recruiting manager who hands off at the offer. A pod lead, running a small team that carries both.
You'll manage the recruiters screening early talent, and you'll manage the fractional HR coordination support that turns an accepted offer into a real employee. Where the program touches the person, you and the Claude Corps program managers work the case together: performance concerns, employee relations, a placement that isn't landing. You bring the process and the employment side. They bring the day-to-day context and the host relationship. Both names are on the outcome.
The math is the other half of the job. We go from 100 fellows to 1,000 to 10,000, and the pod does not grow 100x to match. A team this size clears that volume by building AI into the work: screening support, scheduling, candidate communication, onboarding packets, compliance tracking, the reporting that eats a coordinator's week. We train people to build with AI. We expect the people running our own operations to do the same.
The pod is small in Cohort 1. It grows with the cohorts, and how much it has to grow is partly up to you.
What you will own
Lead the pod . Manage the fractional early-talent recruiters and the HR coordinators supporting Claude Corps. Set the week's priorities, run the load-balancing when a cohort deadline compresses, coach against the bar, and grow the team's headcount and capability as cohorts scale. Fractional support means you are explicit about what you're buying with those hours and what falls to you.
Own screening and selection . Run the funnel from application review through offer, against the program's selection rubric and calibration process. Keep throughput honest: the pod moves volume, and you hold the line on signal quality and candidate experience while it does.
Own the employer-of-record lifecycle . Offers and e-sign, background checks, I-9 and work authorization, payroll setup, benefits enrollment, onboarding. Fellows are CodePath employees, and the experience should feel like it. You direct this work through the fractional coordinators rather than doing all of it yourself.
Use AI to hold the ratio . Find the repetitive work in recruiting and HR ops and get it automated or AI-assisted: resume screening support, interview scheduling, candidate comms, offer and onboarding document generation, multi-state compliance tracking, cohort reporting. Judgment calls stay with humans, and you decide where that line sits. Come with a bias toward trying things, and bring the team along so the whole pod works this way, not just you.
Co-own employee relations and performance with program management . When a fellow's performance or conduct needs attention, you and the program manager run it together. You own documentation, process, consistency, and the employment decisions that follow. The PM owns the host relationship and what's actually happening on the ground. Escalate to the Head of People when the situation warrants it, and know where that line is.
Build the systems . Turn one-cohort processes into repeatable operations: screening workflows, HR SLAs, multi-state compliance, and clean handoffs with our program partners. Bring a point of view on what to standardize and what to leave flexible while the program is still forming

5+ years across recruiting and HR or people operations, including time owning both, not just one
You've managed people, and you've managed through others' capacity, including contractors, shared services, or fractional support
You've run high-volume or early-talent hiring, and you've owned HR operations (payroll, benefits, compliance, onboarding). Employer-of-record, PEO, or multi-state employment experience is a strong plus
You already use AI in your own work and can point to something you automated or rebuilt with it. Comfort with ATS and HRIS configuration, workflow automation, and prompting is expected, not a bonus
You've handled employee relations and performance conversations, and you're steady in them
You're comfortable in a program that is still being built. You bring structure without waiting for someone else to hand it to you
You hold a high bar on quality and candidate experience at the same time
You communicate directly and work well across partner organizations with different systems and cultures
You care about the mission: expanding who gets to build with AI, and doing right by the people you employ
What success looks like
Each cohort is screened and hired on time, at target size, without cutting corners on signal quality
The employment lifecycle runs cleanly: offers, onboarding, payroll, and benefits land on time and compliant across every state we hire in
Cost and hours per fellow hired and onboarded drop cohort over cohort, because the work got automated and not because the team absorbed it
Performance and ER issues get handled early, documented consistently, and resolved with the program manager rather than around them
The pod grows in capability and ownership as the program scales, and the fractional support model either scales with it or you make the case for what replaces it

As a HR SPECIALIST (MILITARY) -Title 32, GS-0201-9, you will provide technical expertise and guidance for all military personnel assigned in the State, and oversees the functions of one of the following human resource programs: Officer Personnel Management (OPM), Enlisted Personnel Management (EPM), Personnel Systems, Integrated Personnel and Pay System - Army (IPPS-A), or the Personnel Services Section.
GENERAL EXPERIENCE: Experience, education or training which provided a general knowledge of principles of organization, management, and administration. Compiling reports, letters, memoranda, etc., and required person-to-person contacts to convey information.

Progressively responsible experience which demonstrates the ability to provide technical guidance and assistance in the type of work or in comparable work of the position to be filled. Experience using computer and automation systems.

SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: To qualify for the GS-0201-09 level, you must have at least 12 months of specialized experience, education or training equivalent to at least the next lower grade level. Applicants must have experience providing technical guidance and assistance in the type of work or in comparable work of the position to be filled.

Applicants must have a thorough knowledge and understanding of administrative procedures and practices of management. Experience developing administrative procedures.

Providing expert technical guidance on complex, controversial, or unprecedented classification issues.
Planning and assigning work, setting priorities, evaluating performance, and/or overseeing the training and development of subordinate HR specialist.
Providing authoritative advisory services to management on organizational design, the impact of reorganizations, and the development of Most Efficient Organizations (MEOs) to ensure sound and effective position structure.
Serving as the subject matter expert on classification appeal procedures, compensation strategies, and the use of automated classification tools and systems.
Developing and/or implementing command-wide human resources policies and programs, ensuring regulatory compliance and operational effectiveness.
Analyzing and/or resolving the most complex and sensitive issues related to position classification, organizational design, and pay administration.
Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected.

See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities.

Current Civilian Employees of the Command (Current CHRA employees): Current Civilian Employees of the Command Domestic Defense Industrial Base/Major Range and Test Facilities Base Civilian Personnel Workforce Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan Land Management Workforce Flexibility Act Military Spouses, under Executive Order (E.O.) 13473 Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Reserve (MR) and National Guard (NG) Technician Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD Military Spouse Preference (MSP) Eligible Priority Placement Program, DoD MR and NG Preference Eligible Tech Receiving Disability Retirement Priority Placement Program, DoD Retained Grade Preference Eligible Veterans Recruitment Appointment (VRA) In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document.

GS-13 Specialized Experience: One year of specialized experience which includes meeting the following: 1) Providing technical advisory services to management on position classification, which includes writing and evaluating position descriptions, applying OPM classification standards and/or guides to determine the correct title, series, and grade, 2) Advising managers on strategic organizational design, career path development, and/or the impact of reorganization on positions, and 3) Resolving complex or controversial classification issues.

This definition of specialized experience is typical of work performed at the next lower grade/level position in the federal service (GS-12). Time in Grade Requirement: Applicants who have held a General Schedule (GS) position within the last 52 weeks must have 52 weeks of Federal service at the next lower grade or equivalent (GS-12).

Qualification requirement: Qualifications must be met by the closing date of this announcement.

Plan, coordinate, and direct personnel functions in the areas of staffing and recruitment.
Exercise supervisory personnel management responsibilities to include evaluating employee performance; overseeing the timely and efficient work of staff; setting and adjusting staff priorities and deadlines; identifying team training needs.
Interpret Federal Human Resources regulations, policies, and procedures, and provide technical guidance to staff.
Mentor subordinates and team members.
Prepare various reports.
Research personnel regulations, laws, and policies
Resolve complex work problems or complaints.
Applicants must meet all qualifications and eligibility requirements by the closing date of the announcement including time-in-grade restrictions, specialized experience and/or education, as defined below.

Time in grade: Applicants must meet one year at the next lower grade to be considered for the next higher grade (e.g. one year at the GS-12 grade level for consideration for the GS-13 grade level.) For the GS-13 level: Applicants must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 level.

Resume must demonstrate at least 4 of the 6 areas below: Planning or directing the operational functions of a Human Resources Staffing and Recruitment program to include managing, supervising or leading subordinate staff. Providing advice and regulatory interpretation in the staffing or recruitment disciplines.

Participating in short or long-range planning groups designed to evaluate operational effectiveness and improve Human Resources processes. Providing technical advice on Federal Human Resources statutes, regulations, laws, and policies.

Representing an Agency at various levels from the Department level on down via both formal and informal presentations and/or communications. Demonstrated understanding of an organization's key personnel and stakeholders and how to cultivate relationships necessary for mission success.

For more information on the qualifications for this position, click here: Human Resources Management Series, 0201 Temporary Promotion Not-to-Exceed: This is a temporary promotion not-to-exceed one year and may be extended up to 5 years without further competition or may end earlier due to lack of work or funds, or at the discretion of the Hiring Manager.

Note: If you are applying at the target grade level identified in the vacancy announcement and you currently hold that same grade level, the personnel action will be processed as a detail instead of a temporary promotion.

This detail may be extended without further competition or may end earlier due to lack of work or funds, or at the discretion of the Hiring Manager. This temporary promotion may be made permanent without further competition.

If the temporary promotion is not made permanent, you will be returned to your permanent position of record with any increases that would have been received if not temporarily assigned.

If it is not possible to be returned to the prior position, you will be placed in another position in your agency for which qualified, at the same grade and geographic location as before. Should this not occur, reduction-in-force procedures may be necessary.

If you are selected, we will work with you and your supervisor on an agreement covering return rights so every effort will be made to return you to a properly classified position for which qualified and at the same grade level. This position is subject to all applicable laws, regulations, and policies under the direction of Agency.

Selection does not restrict the Agency from any future reorganization or realignment efforts. If a change in duty location is required after selection due to a directed reassignment, relocation expenses may be reimbursed. Declination of a directed reassignment could result in your removal from Federal service.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Es ist Feierabend und du verlässt das Office, happy und mit einem guten Gefühl. Dein erster Tag bei PRESCH war einfach stark 🔥
Du hast dein Team kennengelernt, einen ersten Blick in die Personalunterlagen geworfen und die offenen Stellen auf dem Tisch. Du merkst sofort: Hier wird nicht geredet, hier wird gemacht.
Und dir fällt noch etwas auf. Diese Position gibt es bei uns noch nicht. HR läuft bisher nebenbei mit, verteilt auf zwei Schultern, die eigentlich andere Aufgaben haben. Das heißt für dich: Du erbst keine Strukturen, du baust sie.
Wir sind 22 Leute und stellen in den nächsten zwölf Monaten fünf bis zehn weitere ein. Wachstum, keine Nachbesetzung – wir verlieren kaum jemanden. Genau deshalb suchen wir niemanden, der Personalakten sortiert, sondern jemanden, der eine HR-Funktion von der ersten Zeile an aufbaut und danach betreibt 💪
Du berichtest direkt an die Geschäftsführung. Wenn du das schon einmal gemacht hast und wieder machen willst, sollten wir reden.
Aufgaben
🛠️ Du verantwortest unsere Personaladministration komplett. Vorbereitende Lohn- und Gehaltsabrechnung gegenüber unserem Steuerberater, Verträge, digitale Personalakte, Abwesenheiten, Arbeitszeugnisse und Reisekosten. Nicht weiterleiten, sondern verantworten – inklusive Plausibilitätsprüfung, bevor gezahlt wird.
🛠️ Du übernimmst unser Recruiting bis zum Gespräch. Welche Stelle wir besetzen, entscheiden wir. Das Profil, die Seniorität und das Gehaltsband schärfst du gemeinsam mit uns. Ausschreibung, Kanäle, Bewerbermanagement, Vorauswahl und Terminierung laufen dann bei dir. Wir kommen spätestens beim persönlichen Gespräch dazu.
🛠️ Du baust unsere Arbeitgebermarke und eigene Recruiting-Kanäle auf. Karriereseite, Bewertungsprofile, aktive Ansprache. Heute bekommen wir auf eigene Ausschreibungen zu wenige Bewerbungen und kaufen den Rest ein. Das drehst du.
🛠️ Du führst unser HR-System ein. Zeiterfassung, Urlaub, digitale Personalakte. Auswahl, Einführung und Datenübernahme gestaltest du mit – du entscheidest mit, statt ein System zu erben.
🛠️ Du schreibst unsere Prozesse und Richtlinien. Mobiles Arbeiten, Onboarding, Vertragsstruktur. Alles, was heute Einzelfallentscheidung ist, wird bei dir zum Prozess.
🛠️ Du verantwortest den Onboarding-Prozess. Bei diesem Einstellungstempo entscheidet sich Kultur beim Einstieg – nicht erst danach. Die fachliche Einarbeitung bleibt bei den Führungskräften, der Ablauf gehört dir.
🛠️ Du koordinierst und dokumentierst den Arbeitsschutz. Gefährdungsbeurteilungen, Unterweisungen, arbeitsmedizinische Vorsorge und Ersthelfer hältst du organisatorisch nach und dokumentierst sie vollständig. Fachlich arbeitest du dabei mit unseren externen Fachpartnern und den Führungskräften zusammen – als Hersteller von Werkzeug und persönlicher Schutzausrüstung nehmen wir das Thema besonders ernst.
🛠️ Du lieferst der Geschäftsführung Personalkennzahlen. Personalkostenquote, Headcount-Planung, Besetzungsdauer, Krankenquote. Damit wir steuern und nicht schätzen.
Dein Impact nach 12 Monaten
🛠️ Entgelt, Verträge und Abwesenheiten laufen ohne die Geschäftsführung. Wir schauen nur noch auf Freigaben.
🛠️ Unser HR-System ist live, Urlaubsstände sind tagesaktuell abrufbar, die Personalakten sind vollständig digital.
🛠️ Auf unsere Ausschreibungen kommen deutlich mehr passende Bewerbungen als heute. Externe Vermittler brauchen wir nur noch für Spezialistenrollen.
🛠️ Jeder neue Kollege ist ab Tag eins arbeitsfähig: Arbeitsplatz, Zugänge, Material und Einarbeitungsplan stehen vorher.
🛠️ Unsere HR-Prozesse und die Arbeitsschutzdokumentation sind sauber aufgesetzt. Du weißt jederzeit, wo wir stehen.
🛠️ Im Unternehmen bist du die Person, an die alle denken, wenn es um Personalthemen geht.
Qualifikation
🛠️ Mehrjährige Erfahrung als HR-Generalist/in. Breit, nicht spezialisiert – du hast Entgelt, Verträge, Recruiting und Mitarbeiterthemen schon nebeneinander gemacht.
🛠️ Du hast HR schon einmal aufgebaut, nicht nur verwaltet. Ein System eingeführt, Richtlinien geschrieben, Prozesse etabliert. Das ist der wichtigste Punkt in dieser Liste.
🛠️ Vorbereitende Lohn- und Gehaltsabrechnung sitzt. Du hast mit einem externen Lohnbüro oder Steuerberater zusammengearbeitet und die Auswertungen geprüft, statt sie durchzuwinken.
🛠️ Arbeits- und Sozialversicherungsrecht wendest du sicher an. Und du erkennst zuverlässig, wann ein Fall zum Fachanwalt gehört. Beides ist uns gleich wichtig.
🛠️ Recruiting hast du eigenständig geführt. Von der Bedarfsklärung mit dem Fachbereich bis zur Vorauswahl. Du kennst Kanäle, die funktionieren, und weißt, warum manche Ausschreibungen leer bleiben.
🛠️ Du arbeitest eigenverantwortlich. Wir setzen dir keine Aufgaben vor, wir übergeben Verantwortung. Personalentscheidungen treffen wir gemeinsam, den Weg dorthin gestaltest du.
🛠️ Diskretion ist für dich selbstverständlich. Du hast Zugang zu allem. Das setzt Vertrauen voraus, in beide Richtungen.
🛠️ Du nutzt KI als Arbeitswerkzeug – oder willst damit anfangen. Wir arbeiten damit im ganzen Unternehmen. Wenn du schon Vorlagen, Auswertungen oder Abläufe damit gebaut hast: umso besser.
🛠️ Sehr gutes Deutsch. Englisch hilft bei internationalen Themen und Kollegen, ist aber kein Muss-Kriterium.
Bonus: Wenn du eine Richtlinie oder ein Onboarding-Konzept mitbringst, das du selbst geschrieben hast – zeig es uns. Wir wollen sehen, wie du denkst, nicht nur was im CV steht.

🛠️ Du baust deine eigene Funktion auf. Diese Position gibt es bei uns noch nicht. Du entscheidest, wie HR bei PRESCH aussieht – und wohin die Funktion wächst, von der Personalentwicklung bis zur Vergütungsstruktur, gestaltest du mit.
🛠️ Du bist die erste HR-Person bei PRESCH, aber nicht allein. Für Entgelt und steuerliche Fragen steht unser Steuerberater bereit, für arbeitsrechtliche Fälle ein Fachanwalt, und in der Buchhaltung hast du eine Kollegin, die dich vertritt.
🛠️ Gleitzeit. Du willst Job und Familie die gleiche Zeit widmen und sehnst dich daher nach einem flexiblen Arbeitszeitmodell? Kein Problem! Wir integrieren die Arbeit in unser Leben und nicht andersherum.
🛠️ Homeoffice-Tage. Nach der Einarbeitung arbeitest du in Absprache mit dem Team flexibel von zu Hause. Persönlich vor Ort bist du da, wo es zählt: bei Gesprächen, Onboardings und im Austausch mit dem Team.
🛠️ Du willst dich weiterentwickeln, eine Weiterbildung im Arbeitsrecht machen oder auf eine HR-Conference? Alles klar, dann los! Wir legen großen Wert auf deine Weiterbildung und schaffen den finanziellen und zeitlichen Rahmen dafür.
🛠️ Betriebliche Altersvorsorge mit unserem Zuschuss.
🛠️ 30 Tage Urlaub.
🛠️ Mitarbeiterrabatt auf unser komplettes Werkzeugsortiment.
🛠️ Unsere Hierarchien sind flach, der Zusammenhalt ist groß: Wir feiern unseren Erfolg. Wissensaustausch, Glühweinabende, BBQ und regelmäßige Teamevents erwarten dich bei uns. Getränke sind selbstverständlich dabei.
🛠️ Du bist in alle Geschehnisse unseres jungen und wachsenden Unternehmens einbezogen und führst deine eigenen Projekte.
Wenn du HR nicht verwalten, sondern aufbauen willst, freuen wir uns auf dich!

We’re a business navigating a period of transformation and growth, and we know that lasting progress is only possible when the people foundations underneath it are solid. We’re looking for an HR Administrator to be our regional presence in Germany, someone who takes genuine pride in getting the details right and who enjoys being the trusted, go-to person for People and HR matters.
This is a hands-on, varied role covering two connected halves: On the People side, you’ll support the full employee lifecycle for our EU-based population, working closely with, and reporting into, the HR Manager (UK/EU); from onboarding and contracts through to day-to-day queries, payroll inputs, and offboarding.

On the office side, you’ll take ownership of day-to-day administration for our Germany offices, keeping things running smoothly for the team based there.

You’ll be the face of People and HR ATG in Germany: a proactive, organised self-starter who is comfortable working independently, escalating the right things to the HR Manager, and building trusted relationships with employees at every level.
Tasks

· HR Administration & Employee Lifecycle (Germany)

· Act as the first point of contact for Germany-based employees on day-to-day HR queries, policies and procedures, escalating and supporting complex matters with the HR Manager (UK/EU)

· Support the end-to-end employee lifecycle for Germany and EU employees, including onboarding, contract changes, promotions, transfers and offboarding

· Prepare and issue employment contracts, contract amendments and other employment documentation in line with local legal requirements

· Maintain accurate, up-to-date employee records and personnel files for the Germany population, ensuring GDPR compliance

· Coordinate onboarding and induction for new starters in Germany and EU, including right-to-work checks, equipment set up, and welcome activities

· Support recruitment activity for Germany-based roles, including scheduling interviews, liaising with candidates and hiring managers, and maintaining the applicant tracking system

· Prepare and submit monthly Germany payroll inputs (e.g. new starters, leavers, changes), working closely with the HR Manager and the Mexico Service Centre

· Support benefits administration for German employees, including pension, health insurance and other statutory benefits

· Help ensure compliance with German and EU labour law and statutory requirements, flagging risks or changes to the HR Manager (UK/EU)

· Support the administration of performance review cycles and any local training or development activity

· Provide administrative support to the HR Manager on EU and Germany-related HR projects, audits and reporting
Office Administration (Germany)

· Act as the main point of contact for day-to-day office administration in the German offices

· Manage office supplies, equipment and vendor relationships

· Support health & safety compliance for the Berlin office, including risk assessments and fire safety procedures

· Organise office events, socials and wellbeing initiatives for the Berlin team, in partnership with the HR Manager and the wider Employee Experience calendar

· Manage incoming and outgoing post, deliveries, and visitor arrangements for the Berlin office

· Support new starters with desk set up, access passes/keys, and induction to the office

· Liaise with building management/landlord on facilities issues

· Support ad hoc administrative and office management tasks as required

· Some experience in an HR administration, HR coordinator, or office administration role (internships and placements considered)

· Working knowledge of German employment law and HR practices

· Fluent in German and English, both written and spoken

· Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and competing deadlines

· Excellent attention to detail and accuracy, particularly with employee data and documentation

· A proactive, can-do attitude, comfortable working independently as the HR and office presence on the ground in Germany

· Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build trust with employees at all levels

· Ability to manage confidential information with discretion

· Comfortable using HRIS, payroll or office management systems (training provided)

· Studying towards or holding a relevant HR qualification (e.g. IHK Personalfachkaufmann/-frau or equivalent)

· Experience supporting an international or matrixed organisation

· Experience with office management or facilities coordination

Dedicated international team with a flat organizational structure.
Ambitious projects to take ownership of, with a broad scope for co-decision-making.
Fully covered mobility (Deutschlandticket) or Wellbeing (Urban Sports Clubs).
Your well-being matters to us: take care of your mental health through a variety of classes, trainings and sessions with OpenUp.
Flexible working setup to make the most of your working hours: we offer flexibility in our Hybrid/Remote model; however, we do expect you to use our Berlin office in Charlottenburg 2 days per week.
Work from abroad fully remote for up to 30 working days per year.
Dog-friendly office: we can’t wait to meet your furry friend!
Of course, we have regular get-togethers, company events, and drinks and snacks you can enjoy at our office.

This position will be assigned to the centralized Child & Youth (CY) background check investigation cell within the Air Force Services Center (AFSVC).

The incumbent of this position will function as the Senior Human Resources Specialist and technical expert for the background check investigation cell, which will provide a centralized administrative process for completing and making fitness determinations for child and youth (CY) background checks.

The incumbent of this position will direct the flow of work and may be required to perform lead-type duties (i.e., directing the flow of work for a team/cell), as needed.

The incumbent administers the security program for Non-Appropriated Funds (NAF), implements fitness-for-duty policies and procedures in accordance with applicable guidelines, and monitors the suitability/fitness program for consistency with applicable laws.

Additionally, the incumbent distributes updates in policy and/or procedures for background check investigations for child and youth positions to installation-level NAF Human Resources (HR) offices, briefs installations and the functional community on established policies and procedures, delivers technical expertise in automated security administration systems, and resolves and troubleshoots system errors and malfunctions.

They provide guidance/assistance on unique scenarios to local NAF HR offices, conduct training on background check investigation requirements, and review findings from background checks to include Installation Records Checks and fingerprint results.

The incumbent requests case files and applicable information to make a fitness determination and authorizes Line of Sight Supervision (LOSS) during prescreening as an interim determination.

The incumbent also interviews individuals to gather information concerning derogatory information found during the investigation, evaluates all information (favorable and unfavorable) to make fitness determinations for childcare positions, and provides justification for fitness determination decisions.

They ensure determinations are disseminated to the appropriate installations with follow-on procedures for the local NAF HR office to execute, provide procedures on disputing or appealing fitness determination decisions, and recommend decisions to refer cases to a higher entity for further investigation when there is evidence of intentional false statements, deception, or fraud.

Finally, the incumbent performs administrative security personnel work, ensures that installation records checks with questionable information or derogatory findings are provided or forwarded to the proper investigating entity (i.e., OPM or DoD), and performs other related duties as assigned.

Im Generalsekretariat der Bildungsdirektion suchen wir ab sofort oder nach Vereinbarung eine/n HR\-/IT\-Projektmanager/in mit einem Pensum von 80%\-100%.
### Ihr Aufgabengebiet
Sie gestalten die digitale Transformation unserer HR\-Systemlandschaft aktiv mit und übernehmen eine zentrale bei der Einführung und Weiterentwicklung von SAP SuccessFactors. Als Projektleiterin oder Projektleiter für die Bildungsdirektion begleiten Sie die Einführung und Weiterentwicklung des Systems und stehen den HR\-Mitarbeitenden dabei beratend und unterstützend zur Seite.
In Ihrer Stabsstelle sind Sie direkt der Co\-Leitung HR\-Services (HRS) unterstellt. Neben der Einführung und Weiterentwicklung der neuen HR\-Systemlandschaft unterstützen Sie das HRS\-Team und die Abteilung bei weiteren HR\-Projekten.

Sie gestalten die Weiterentwicklung und Vereinheitlichung von HR\-Prozessen aktiv mit, bewirtschaften die Personalhomepage und bearbeiten die eingehenden Tickets im ServiceNow. Dabei lösen Sie Anfragen selbstständig oder koordinieren deren Weiterleitung an die zuständigen Stellen.
Je nach Aufgabe übernehmen Sie die Verantwortung für Projekte und Teilprojekte oder wirken unterstützend an deren Umsetzung mit. Sie behalten den Überblick, koordinieren die verschiedenen Aktivitäten und sorgen dafür, dass alle relevanten Anspruchsgruppen frühzeitig und angemessen eingebunden werden.

Als kompetente Ansprechperson bearbeiten Sie interne und externe Anfragen, präsentieren Ergebnisse und moderieren Sitzungen sowie Workshops. Darüber hinaus entwickeln Sie Konzepte und bringen Ihre Fachkompetenz bei abteilungsinternen Fragestellungen und Aufträgen ein.
### Ihr Profil
Für diese vielseitige Funktion suchen wir eine engagierte Persönlichkeit die Erfahrung an der Schnittstelle zwischen IT und HR mitbringt. Sie haben bereits mit SAP SuccessFactors gearbeitet oder eine entsprechende Einführung begleitet und verfügen über eine Ausbildung im Projektmanagement. Erfahrung in der öffentlichen Verwaltung setzen wir voraus.
Sie kommunizieren gerne und verfügen über ausgeprägte zwischenmenschliche Fähigkeiten. Gleichzeitig zeichnen Sie sich durch Umsetzungsstärke und Durchsetzungsvermögen aus. Mit Ihrer begeisterungsfähigen, initiativen und engagierten gelingt es Ihnen, andere für neue Themen zu gewinnen und Veränderungen aktiv mitzugestalten.
Eine ausgeprägte Dienstleistungs\- und Kundenorientierung ist für Sie selbstverständlich. Sie arbeiten gerne im Team, übernehmen Verantwortung und begegnen Veränderungen offen, flexibel und lösungsorientiert. Zudem verfügen Sie über ausgeprägte konzeptionelle und analytische Fähigkeiten und verstehen es, komplexe Zusammenhänge zu erfassen, innovative Ideen zu entwickeln und diese gemeinsam mit anderen erfolgreich in die Praxis umzusetzen.
### Unser Angebot
Wir bieten Ihnen eine abwechslungsreiche und verantwortungsvolle Tätigkeit in einem dynamischen Umfeld. Sie erhalten Freiraum für eigene Ideen und die Möglichkeit, Ihre Expertise wirkungsvoll einzubringen und die Weiterentwicklung unserer HR\-Systemlandschaft aktiv mitzugestalten.
Sie werden Teil eines engagierten Teams, in dem gegenseitige Unterstützung und eine gute Zusammenarbeit grossgeschrieben werden. Flexible Arbeitszeiten, eine moderne Infrastruktur und attraktive Anstellungsbedingungen runden unser Angebot ab.
